summary.text: The halogens are group 17 of the periodic table: fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine, astatine and tennessine.
The word halogen means salt former, because halogens react with metals to produce salts such as table salt, sodium chloride.
All of them form acids when bonded to hydrogen, and the middle halogens, chlorine, bromine and iodine, are often used as disinfectants.

facts.label: States of matter
facts.value: Only group with elements in three main states at standard conditions

items.prompt: Halogens are named for what they make when they meet metals. Which item on a kitchen table is one such product?
items.explain: When halogens react with metals they produce salts, including sodium chloride, common table salt.

items.prompt: A cleaner wants a disinfectant from the halogen group. Which elements are the usual picks?
items.explain: The middle halogens, chlorine, bromine and iodine, are often used as disinfectants.

items.prompt: Scheele made chlorine in 1774 but did not realise it was an element. Who later showed that it was?
items.explain: In 1807 Humphry Davy investigated chlorine and discovered that it is an actual element.

items.prompt: While making saltpeter, a chemist adds sulfuric acid to boiled seaweed ash and gets purple fumes that condense into black crystals. Which halogen has he found?
items.explain: Courtois found that adding sulfuric acid produced purple fumes that condensed into black crystals, which proved to be the new element iodine.

items.prompt: Some authors leave tennessine out of the halogens. What is their reason?

options.label: It forms no salts with metals
It was named for a mineral, not a place
It is not radioactive, unlike the others
Its chemistry is unknown and expected to resemble gallium's

items.explain: Its chemistry is unknown and is theoretically expected to be more like that of gallium.

items.prompt: Fluorine's name comes from a Latin word meaning to flow. Where does that link come from?

options.label: It came from a mineral used as a flux in metalworking
It is a liquid at room temperature
It was first found in flowing river water
It dissolves quickly in any water

items.explain: Fluorine was derived from the mineral fluorite, which was used as a flux in metalworking.
